open_points.subject: K-11 MCP surface
open_points.text: The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.
open_points.question: How are the primary actions to add or capture a trial case, release a failed run, roll back a slot, propose a binding, compose and prove a flow, and refuse an effect exposed, given that they are absent from the stated fixed MCP operation set?
options: Each is a distinct omitted MCP operation
Some are modes of the named operations
They are not available through MCP
open_points.default_guess: Treat every primary action as an MCP operation and regard K-11's list as accidentally incomplete.

open_points.subject: read-only flow activation
open_points.text: A proven read-only flow is activated by the kernel as soon as the owner or an agent asks for it (the action "activate a flow"); any other flow only by the owner. / The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.
open_points.question: May an agent invoke the activation action for a proven read-only flow, or is activation exposed only as an owner action?
options: An agent or the owner may request read-only activation
Only the owner may request any activation
Agents activate read-only flows through a different named operation
open_points.default_guess: Allow an agent or the owner to request activation of a proven read-only flow.

open_points.subject: try an implementation action
open_points.text: try an implementation | agent | trial evidence per case
open_points.question: Does one try request execute the implementation against every active trial case, one caller-selected case, or a caller-selected subset?
options: Run every active case
Run one selected case
Run a selected subset of cases
open_points.default_guess: Run every active case and create one TrialExecution per case.

open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict
open_points.text: Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict. / every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions.
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is a new AdmissionVerdict created for the new TrialExecutions and `decided_at`, or is the existing verdict reused despite the required rerun?
options: Create a new entity verdict for each admission run
Reuse one value verdict and replace or append its evidence
Keep one content verdict while recording each admission run as a separate model
open_points.default_guess: Create a distinct admission-run entity each time so its executions and decision time remain unambiguous.

open_points.subject: M09 Activation after trial-corpus growth
open_points.text: The current activation of a contract version is the one recorded last. / Read by activation, which requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus. / a failed real execution can be captured into it, so a repaired slot stays repaired.
open_points.question: What happens to an existing activation when a trial case is added and its implementation has no admitted verdict over the enlarged current corpus?
options: It remains active and runnable
It remains recorded but cannot be used by new runs until readmitted
The kernel automatically readmits it and either keeps or removes activation
Adding the case immediately removes or supersedes the activation
open_points.default_guess: Follow the stated activation lifecycle literally: leave it active and runnable, while requiring the enlarged corpus only for later submissions and rollbacks.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult
open_points.text: Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result. / whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can first be unproven and later proven after a referenced binding changes from proposed to accepted?
options: ProofResult identity includes the relevant dependency state
Each proof computation is a separate entity observation
ProofResult is an ephemeral value identified only by its complete returned facts
The earlier result is replaced by the later result
open_points.default_guess: Treat each on-demand result as an ephemeral value identified by its complete facts, not by `flow_version_id` alone.

open_points.subject: M23 NodeExecution
open_points.text:
### Identity

value / an attempt's record is issued once. Continuity: none; a further attempt is a further record.
open_points.question: Is NodeExecution a value or an issued entity observation, and what exact facts mint or identify it?
options: An entity identified by the run/node/map-index/attempt-number tuple
An entity with a separately minted execution id
A content-derived value including all observation facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`, consistently with TrialExecution being an observation.

open_points.subject: M14 map and port cardinality
open_points.text: `map_over`: the one input port a `many` edge maps the node over, when mapped. The node runs once per element in list order (a `many` value is a list); every other input is given the same value for every element; each output collects one result per element in that order.
open_points.question: Which model fact is `many` during a map—the source port, the destination node input port, the edge, or an effective mapped-node port—and does each NodeExecution and captured TrialCase contain one element or the whole collection for that input?
options: A `many` source feeds a `one` destination input one element per execution
The destination input is declared `many` but each execution receives one element
Both endpoint ports are `many`, with map changing their per-execution shape
The edge has an independent cardinality fact
open_points.default_guess: Use a `many` source feeding a `one` destination input; each execution and captured case receives the single element, and mapped outputs are collected by the flow.

open_points.subject: capture failed execution
open_points.text: an execution that succeeded, was skipped, belongs to another contract version, or whose run was already released (its files are gone) is refused / A file moves between nodes through a spool that belongs to its run and is emptied when the run ends — except a `failed` run
open_points.question: Can an unsuccessful function execution be captured after its run ended `refused`, `cancelled`, or `succeeded`, given that such a run was not released but its file spool has already been removed?
options: Capture is allowed only while every required input payload still exists
Capture is allowed only from an active or final `failed` unreleased run
Value-only executions remain capturable after other final statuses, but file-input executions do not
Any non-released run remains capturable despite spool removal
open_points.default_guess: Allow capture only while all required input payloads still exist; therefore value-only captures may survive, but captures needing removed spool files are refused.

open_points.subject: M24 request_digest and credentials
open_points.text: `request_digest`: the digest of the fully built request shown; the approval covers that request only / The credential's value is never shown, so rotating it voids nothing.
open_points.question: Does `request_digest` include credential-bearing header values, and if not, what credential-independent representation is part of the approved request facts?
options: Exclude credential values and digest a stable placeholder or credential reference
Include credential values, so rotation invalidates approval
Exclude all credential-bearing headers from the digest
Maintain separate shown-request and send-request digests
open_points.default_guess: Exclude credential values while retaining the header's identity through a stable placeholder, so rotation does not change the approval digest.

open_points.subject: M18, M19 and M26 flow-activation authority
open_points.text: for a `draft-write` send the flow activation under which the run started / a flow activation by its position in the store's order / `flow_version_id`: pinned at start
open_points.question: How does a Run retain the exact FlowActivation identity needed later as a draft-write EffectAttempt's authority, especially when the same version can be activated more than once?
options: Run explicitly pins the FlowActivation's store position
Run pins only the version and the activation is reconstructed from store order and start time
EffectAttempt discovers and stores the activation only when sending
Version identity alone is treated as sufficient authority
open_points.default_guess: Have the Run explicitly pin the exact FlowActivation store position at start.

open_points.subject: M27 Actor and automatic records
open_points.text: its records name it as the actor, so no automatic step looks like a human decision. / A record with no by-field (AdmissionVerdict, NodeExecution, EffectAttempt apart from its `resolved_by`, an EffectApproval until decided, StoredValue, SpooledFile) is the kernel's own work
open_points.question: Must every kernel-created record explicitly carry `Actor{kind: kernel}`, or does absence of an actor field represent kernel authorship?
options: Every relevant record explicitly names the kernel actor
Absence of a by-field denotes the kernel
Only automatic decision records name the kernel; mechanical records omit actors
open_points.default_guess: Explicitly record the kernel actor for automatic decisions and actions, following K-15's requirement that records name it.
